evidence: Figure 1.1 caption: "the canonical model has 64 query and 64 KV heads per layer (Ch. 4, Table 4-2 — [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], the book's constructed teaching baseline, not a vendor checkpoint), so the four drawn heads stand for the enumeration, not the model's head count." Table 4-2 (p. 80-81) confirms "Reference geometry — query heads (n_heads) 64 [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]" with "under full-MHA every query head carries its own K,V, so n_KV-heads = n_heads = 64" and "Reference geometry — head dim (d_head) 128 ... 64 query heads × head_dim 128 = 8,192 = hidden dim". Figure 1.1's own caption text (p. 34) also draws "layer L · h₁–h₄" for both stored K and stored V.
issue: Figure 1.1 is described in its caption as a "single-layer detail view: one layer's stored K and stored V drawn separately, each enumerated per head (h₁–h₄)" — i.e. the figure draws four head glyphs for a layer whose K/V head set is 64. The caption explicitly acknowledges this ("the four drawn heads stand for the enumeration, not the model's head count") but does not state that the figure's per-layer enumeration is an abbreviation of a 64-head set in the drawn labels themselves; the labels 'h₁–h₄' read as a literal, complete enumeration on the face of the diagram, and the caption's clarification arrives only in the prose. A reader consulting the figure in isolation (or in grayscale, where no head-count cue exists) can carry '4 heads per layer' into the KV arithmetic.
fix_instruction: In Fig 1.1's caption or an in-figure annotation, state explicitly that the h₁–h₄ glyphs represent a 64-head K/V set per layer (canonical geometry, Table 4-2), e.g. label the heads 'h₁…h₆₄ (4 of 64 shown)'. Do not change the KV arithmetic elsewhere — the 2.62 MB/token constant in Table 4-2 already uses the 64-head full-MHA width correctly.
